absent: Interpreter and just in time implementation of branch and load semantics beyond what the vectors imply.
Numeric encodings of opcodes, registers, mode flags, and error codes.
Driver loop, selection, execution, and comparison logic that consumes the table.
Internals of per vector generation callbacks and maximum size construction.
Locking, concurrency, memory management, and lifecycle rules.
Fragment reassembly and packet buffer layout outside the sparse bytes shown.

findings.text: Each vector combines a descriptive label with an instruction store offering an internal form and a classic form, a mode word selecting INTERNAL or CLASSIC execution plus modifiers such as FLAG_NO_DATA plus handling for FLAG_EXPECTED_FAIL and for FLAG_SKB_FRAG, sparse input bytes, ordered expected outcome pairs of length and value, an optional program generation callback referenced by fill_helper, optional fragment bytes referenced by frag_data, and an optional expected error referenced by expected_errcode.

Internal jump vectors follow an initialize, load, branch, exit cycle. The result holder R0 is preset, operands in R1 and also in R2 are loaded including wide sixty four bit forms, a conditional or unconditional transfer either falls through to immediate termination or diverts to an alternate path that revises the result and then terminates. Both forward skips and backward loops are represented.

Branch coverage spans equality, inequality, unsigned ordering, signed ordering, bit presence testing, and unconditional transfer signaled by BPF_JA. Immediate operand and register operand encodings are both exercised, with taken and not taken outcomes distinguished by the final result value, including unsigned treatment of negative bit patterns and strict versus non strict boundary equality.

Wide immediate loads through BPF_LD_IMM64 occupy two instruction positions. Branch displacements in the vectors account for that width when skipping over one or two wide loads, when landing directly on termination, and when selecting between successive constant loads that differ only in low bits.

Classic load vectors follow a preset, fetch, return cycle. An index holder is optionally preset through BPF_LDX, then a one, two, or four byte fetch through BPF_LD occurs by absolute position or by index plus signed adjustment, drawing from linear packet bytes or fragment bytes, followed by return through BPF_RET of the accumulator holder.

Classic load edge behavior is pinned down. Unaligned multi byte reads assemble bytes in packet order, out of range accesses produce a zero value with reduced length, missing index presets behave as a defined default, mixed linear and fragment spans combine head and fragment bytes, repeated indexed fetches reuse the same index, and link layer adjustments through SKF_LL_OFF shift the effective position.

Oversized programs and certain jumps spanning specialized packet operations are rejected with EINVAL instead of executing. The table marks such vectors as expected failures while neighboring maximal size vectors for gap jumps, very long forward and backward transfers, edge hopping, context heavy and call heavy transforms, and literal heavy sequences are expected to succeed.

The fragment relies on stable symbolic categories for execution mode, packet fetch width, addressing mode, return source, general registers, and test modifiers. Modes distinguish internal and classic execution, widths distinguish BPF_B fetches and BPF_H fetches and BPF_W fetches, addressing distinguishes BPF_ABS forms from BPF_IND forms, and modifiers distinguish absent data and expected failure and fragmented input.

The vector collection tests acts as parameterized input to an external driver that selects the active instruction form by mode, builds programs directly or through the per vector generation callback, supplies linear and fragment bytes, executes under internal or classic semantics, and compares observed length and value pairs against the expected pairs.
